1.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties at length, we find that there are two sets of private Imrankhan Ashrafkhan Gangad vs State Of Gujarat on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38233708/
1 persons, namely, the petitioners herein and respondents No.4 and 5, who claim that the plots belonging to them had been utilized/acquired by the National Highway Authority of India (in short as "NHAI") for construction of Ahmedabad Dholera Expressway (National Highway No.751).

sentences.text:
2. The petitioner is purchaser/owner of Survey Nos.258, 265, 266, 264 (old Revenue Survey No.96 )
and have filed the writ petition with the assertion that the officials of the NHAI had illegally entered into the aforesaid plots belonging to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED:
13/02/2024 undefined petitioner on and after 31.05.2022 and were trying to take possession of the aforesaid lands in question, which were in the possession of the petitioner herein.

3. Relief has been sought in the writ petition that respondent No.3, namely NHAI be restrained from interfering with the possession of the petitioner qua land being Revenue Survey Nos.258,264, 265 and 266(old Revenue Survey No.96 Paiki) of village; Jalalpur Godhneshwar, Taluka: Dholka,
District:
Ahmedabad without adopting due process of law.

4. The respondents No.4 and 5, on the other hand, are claiming that their lands in Survey Nos.259,260,286 and 287, which were shown in the acquisition Notification under Section 3A and 3D, actual possession of which, had been taken by the NHAI, are the acquired lands and they are entitled for compensation.

5. We may note that looking to the rival claims of the parties about the actual position of the plots acquired by NHAI, the compensation has been deposited in the Treasury by the competent authority and is lying therein.

6. It is vehemently contended by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the lands in Survey Nos.258,264,265 and 266 (Old Survey No.96 Paiki) of Village: Jalalpur Godhneshwar,
Taluka: Dholka, District: Ahmedabad was never part of the acquisition proceedings.

They were never NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined indicated as the acquired land in the Notifications published under Sections 3A and 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The amended paragraphs of the writ petition have been placed before us to assert that owing to the resurvey conducted by the respondent No.2, the location of the aforesaid plots of the petitioner has been shown at different places and the same were not matching with the four directions of the description of the lands as mentioned in the sale deeds.

Upon getting the said information with regard to the error in the resurvey and mismatching of the lands in question, the petitioner herein had approached the Deputy Director, Land Records, Ahmedabad for correction of the revenue records and his application was allowed vide order dated 19.08.2020.
Pursuant to the said order, Entry No.2800 was mutated, wherein the correction was clearly shown.

7. The contention is that the entire survey made by the respondent No.3, namely the NHAI was based on the faulty records and, hence, the petitioner herein had to approach the respondent No.2 for correction of such errors, and the proposed road line is passing through the lands of the petitioner bearing Survey Nos.258,264, 265 and 266, in spite of the same having not been shown in Imrankhan Ashrafkhan Gangad vs State Of Gujarat on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38233708/
2

sentences.text: the acquisition Notifications under Sections 3A and 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined 8.

In the main writ petition in paragraph No.3.11, it was contended that on 31.05.2022, the officials of the respondent no.3 (NHAI) came along with the police force on the aforesaid lands of the petitioner for the purpose of taking possession.

In the amended paragraph No.3.16, it is, however,
contended that on 27.05.2023, the officials of NHAI had started work on the lands of the petitioner by deploying heavy machinery by including the lands of the petitioner in the acquisitions process and, therefore, the petitioner filed representation on 28.05.2023.

No heed has been paid and the lands of the petitioners have been taken without following due process of law, without giving compensation to the petitioner, which violates their right to property guaranteed under Article 300A of the Constitution of India.

9. Taking note of the said assertions, we may record that the present petition has been presented on 06.05.2023 with the following reliefs: -
"(A) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to allow and admit this petition;
(B) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, and further be set-aside impugned action of respondent No.3 of proposing to acquire lands being Revenue Survey No.258,265,266 and 264( Old Revenue Survey No.96 Paiki) of Village Jalalpur, Godhneshwar, Taluka: Dholka,
District: Ahmedabad further be pleased to restrain respondent no.3 from taking over possession of land in question without following due process of law:
(C) Pending hearing and final disposal of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined present petitioner YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to restrain respondent no.3 from interfering with the possession of petitioner qua lands being Revenue Survey No.258,265, 266 and 264( Old Revenue Survey No.96 Paiki) of Village Jalalpur Godhneshwar, Ta.
Dholka, District: Ahmedabad without following due process of law;"
10.

From the contention made in paragraph No.3.11 it may be noted that as per the case of the petitioner, the officials of respondent No.3 had entered into the lands of the petitioner on 31.05.2022 to take possession thereof.

However, there is no clarity as to why the petitioners would approach the District Inspector of Land Records (in short as "DILR"), Ahmedabad for correction of revenue record by moving application prior to the said date, which has led to passing of order dated 19.08.2020 and correction of the mutation entry.
What prompted the petitioner to seek correction of the record, when his lands were neither acquired nor possession of it was taken, could not be explained.
Even the assertions made in the amended paragraph of the writ petition are not an answer to the said query.

sentences.text: It is further pointed out by learned counsel for the private respondents No.4 and 5 the that the order of the DILR dated 19.08.2020 of correction of records passed in favour of the petitioner had been recalled by the Superintendent of Land Records vide order dated 03.11.2020 and the matter was NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined remanded to the DILR for reconsideration.

In a further order dated 28.10.2021, noticing that the petitioner was present on the site, but he could not co-relate his possession over the acquired land, previous village map (position of records) has been restored by the DILR, thus, restoring the original position of the acquired land, which as per the contention of the respondents No.4 and 5 belong to them.

Learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5 would submit that the lands bearing Survey Nos.286 and 287 included in the acquisition Notifications under Sections 3A and 3D belong to respondents No.4 and 5, and possession of the same has been taken for construction of National Highway.
12.
In the affidavit of respondents No.4 and 5 it is asserted that they and other owners of the lands were having ancestral lands bearing Survey No.96 Paiki with different Khata numbers.

In the promulgation of the Village, Revenue Survey No.96 Paiki, had been divided in many parts as per the share and Khata numbers of different owners and new Survey numbers had been generated Khatawise.
As per the promulgation scheme, new Survey No.286, Khata No.285 was allotted to respondent No.4 and new Survey No.287 (Khata No.286) has been allotted to respondent No.5 herein).
The mutation entry No.2386 had been made in view of the Revenue records on 05.10.2015 to this effect.

The petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED:
13/02/2024 undefined had purchased the land in in Survey No.258,264, 265, 266 in the year 2019,
after the publication of the acquisition Notifications under Sections 3A and 3D dated 23.03.2018 and 23.08.2018; respectively, from the original owners.

Much after the promulgation order, the dispute was sought to be raised by the petitioner by filing application for correction of the map in the year 2020 based on false assertions in order to seek compensation.
The NHAI has already taken possession of the lands belonging to the respondents No.4 and 5 much earlier and there is no question to take over the possession of the lands of the petitioner.

13. We may also take note of the stand of the NHAI, namely respondent No.2, wherein it is categorically stated that as per the acquisition Notifications, Revenue Survey Nos.259,260, 286 and 287 of the village: Jalalpur, Godhneshwar, Taluka:
Dholka, District: Ahmedabad were acquired for construction of National Highway and the said lands were vested with the Central Government free from any encumbrances which became absolute owners of the lands in question.
The purchases made by the petitioner are after completion of the acquisition process and vesting of the acquired lands.

Subsequent to the completion of the acquisition process, the petitioner is trying to raise a dispute with regard to the actual location of the acquired lands, i.e. Revenue Survey NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined Nos.259,260,286 and 287 vis-a-vis the lands purchased by the petitioner in Survey Nos.258,264,265, 266.
In view of the dispute raised by the petitioner, the compensation amount has been deposited by the competent authority in the Treasury and has not been disbursed to anyone.

4 14.

sentences.text: The counsel for the NHAI, would vehemently submit that the NHAI has taken possession of the acquired lands and the contention of the petitioner that their lands though not acquired has been taken away during the construction of the National Highway is without any basis.
The dispute with regard to the mistake in the revenue records is not at all the concern of the NHAI.
The alignment of road has not been changed and the constructions have been made only by utilization of the acquired lands.
The contention that the petitioner had been dispossessed without adopting due process of law is false and without any basis.

15. The question before us is as to who would be entitled for compensation pursuant to two sets of acquisitions Notifications dated 23.03.2018 and 23.08.2018 under Sections 3A and 3D and 08.12.2020 and 13.04.2021, pursuant to which the compensation awards were passed on 08.01.2019 and 07.09.2021; respectively.

16. The factual controversy sought to be raised before us by the petitioner is about the correct location of the plots, which NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined were acquired for the purpose of construction of NH.No.751 and the entitlement of the private parties for compensation.

17. It may further be noted that in the affidavit filed by the Collector dated 13.12.2023 pursuant to the order dated 17.10.2023 passed by us, it is stated that in compliance of the order of this Court, the measurement process was conducted on 30.11.2023,
wherein the details of the lands bearing Revenue Survey No.258,264, 256 and 266 varies from the particulars of the said land indicated in the sale deed dated 08.01.2019 executed in favour of the petitioner herein.
There is a discrepancy in the actual measurement of Revenue Survey Nos. 258,264, 256 and 266 vis-a-vis the measurements as narrated in the sale deed executed in favour of the petitioner herein.

It is stated that there is a dispute regarding location, identification and possession of the lands bearing Survey No. 258,264, 256 and 266 between the petitioner and the private respondents No.4 and 5.

The map which is appended with the said affidavit is sought to be placed before us by the learned Assistant Government Pleader to assert that the position has been clarified after re- measurement of the sites in question after 30.11.2023.
18.

Having noted the above, we find that the factual controversy with regard to the location of the lands of Survey Nos.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined 258,264,265,266, which were purchased by the petitioner herein and, which, according to the petitioner, had been utilized by the NHAI for construction of NH.No.751 without acquisition,
whereas Survey no.259,260,286 and 287, which were included in the acquisition Notifications under Section 3A and 3D published under the National Highways Act, 1956, cannot be decided Imrankhan Ashrafkhan Gangad vs State Of Gujarat on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38233708/
5 within the scope of Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
19.

sentences.text: In our considered opinion, the position, as occurring before us, would require leading of evidence and factual inquiry on the evidence led by the rival parties and as such cannot be adjudicated within the scope of the writ jurisdiction.

The possession memo of the lands in question,
prepared by the competent authority pursuant to the acquisition Notification is also not on record.
20. The relief prayed by the petitioner in the writ petition being outside the scope of the writ jurisdiction, the only remedy available to the petitioner is to approach the Civil Court.
The controversy raised in the writ petition cannot be decided by the competent authority under the National High Way Act or the revenue authorities.
It is, however, clarified that, in case, the petitioner approaches the Civil Court, it shall decide the controversy independently without being influenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9408/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024
undefined 21
. With the above observations, the writ petition stands disposed of.
